name: cropper
title: Image Cropper
description: An image cropper: a photo sits in a rounded frame with a fixed square outline and everything outside it dimmed. Dragging moves the picture beneath the square and scrolling or pinching zooms it.
use: A user must choose the visible part of a photo before it is saved or uploaded.
avoid: The crop is always a square with no ratio control, and it needs a real image URL to show anything.
a11y: Dragging and scrolling are the only controls, so keyboard users cannot pan or zoom; a hidden description is supplied for screen readers. (keyboard: no, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A photograph of mountains above clouds inside a rounded rectangle about 16 by 10. A thin white square outline sits centrally with everything outside it darkened, and a small grey instruction line runs underneath.
behaves: Dragging pans the photo beneath the stationary crop square, while scrolling or pinching zooms it between set limits. The white square never changes size; only the image moves and scales.
customise: The image URL and zoom limits are props; the crop square, dimmed overlay and frame styling are changed through classes on the four sub-parts.
weight: moderate: One large image with pointer-driven transforms; nothing loops until the user drags.
demo: A snow-capped mountain range over a sea of clouds at sunset, captioned 'Drag to reposition · Scroll to zoom'.
issues: The crop is always square; no aspect ratio is offered
The instruction caption below the image is very small and low contrast
polishWhy: Clean photo and a clear white crop edge; no ratio control and the hint text is tiny.
